{{< include _elements-kit.qmd >}}

The whole of [Texture](elements-texture.qmd) on one sheet, the way the school handout lays it out. Every ▶ plays the
example; most use the same two [measures]{.nn} of *Twinkle, Twinkle* so you hear only the texture change. Press
**Full screen** to put the sheet on the whole screen for revision or for the class board.

## The sheet

::::::: {.el-sheet .column-page data-title="Texture: how the layers fit together"}
:::::: {.el-grid}

::::: {.el-card}
#### Monophonic
<p>One line only. Any number of players, as long as they all play the same part. No chords.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="96" data-width="190"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G
G G d d|e e d2|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Octaves
<p>The same tune in two parts, an octave apart: same note names, different pitch. Still one line, heavier.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="96" data-width="190"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G
[G,G] [G,G] [Dd] [Dd]|[Ee] [Ee] [Dd]2|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Homophonic
<p>All parts move <strong>together in the same rhythm</strong>, as chords. Like a hymn. <em>Homo-phonic</em>: "same sound".</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="80" data-width="190"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G
V:1
[DG] [DG] [Gd] [Gd]|[Ge] [Ge] [Fd]2|]
V:2 clef=bass
[G,,B,] [G,,B,] [G,,B,] [G,,B,]|[C,C] [C,C] [D,A,]2|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Melody and accompaniment
<p>A tune, with chords or a pattern underneath supporting it. The most common texture in pop.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="96" data-width="190"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G
V:1
G G d d|e e d2|]
V:2 clef=bass
[G,,D,]2 [G,,D,]2|[C,G,]2 [G,,D,]2|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Polyphonic
<p>Two or more <strong>independent</strong> lines, each a tune (counterpoint). Copying each other is <strong>imitation</strong>; a round is strict imitation.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="100" data-width="190"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Frère Jacques as a round
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G
V:1
G A B G|B c d2|]
V:2
z4|G A B G|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Who does what
<ul>
<li><strong>Melody</strong>: the tune</li>
<li><strong>Accompaniment</strong>: the parts supporting it</li>
<li><strong>Countermelody</strong>: a second tune that fits with the main one</li>
<li><strong>Bass line</strong>: the lowest part</li>
</ul>
<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="96" data-width="190"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Tune, countermelody above, bass line
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G
V:1
b2 a2|g2 f2|]
V:2
G G d d|e e d2|]
V:3 clef=bass
G,,2 B,,2|C,2 D,2|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Call and response
<p>One performer or group plays a phrase; another answers. Blues, gospel, work songs, African music, pop.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="104" data-width="190"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G
V:1
G G d d|z4|]
V:2 clef=bass
z4|E, E, D,2|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Antiphonal
<p>Two groups answering each other from <strong>different places</strong>, such as two choirs on opposite sides of a church.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="100" data-width="190"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G
V:1
[GB] [GB] [Ad] [Ad]|z4|[GB] [Ac] [Bd]2|z4|]
V:2
z4|[GB] [GB] [Ad] [Ad]|z4|[GB] [Ac] [Bd]2|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Pedal
<p>A long or repeated note, usually in the bass, held while the chords change above it.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="96" data-width="190"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G
V:1
[GB] [GB] [Ac] [Ac]|[FA] [FA] [GB]2|]
V:2 clef=bass
D, D, D, D,|D, D, D,2|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Drone
<p>Long or repeated notes, usually two a 5th apart, as on bagpipes.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="96" data-width="190"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G
V:1
G G d d|e e d2|]
V:2 clef=bass
[G,,D,]4|[G,,D,]4|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Alberti bass
<p>A Classical piano accompaniment: each chord broken into four equal notes, <strong>lowest, highest, middle, highest</strong>.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="100" data-width="190"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G
V:1
G G d d|e e d2|]
V:2 clef=bass
L:1/8
G,DB,D G,DB,D|C,G,E,G, G,DB,D|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Basso continuo
<p>Baroque: a bass instrument (cello, bass viol, bassoon) plays the bass line while a harpsichord, organ or lute fills in chords, read from <strong>figured bass</strong>.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="92" data-width="190" data-sound="harpsichord"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:G
V:1
d2 BG TA3 G|G8|]
V:2 clef=bass
[G,,G,]2 [B,,D]2 [C,E]2 [D,C]2|[G,,B,]8|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card .el-wide}
#### Check yourself
<div class="eq" data-set="texture"></div>
:::::

::::::
:::::::

## Describing texture

- Name it, then describe it: *thin* or *thick*, *sparse* or *dense*, how many parts.
- Say what changes, in order: "It starts **monophonic** (a solo flute), becomes **homophonic** when the choir comes in,
  and the middle is **polyphonic**, the voices entering one by one in **imitation**."
- The longer lesson, with fuller examples: [Elements 10: Texture](elements-texture.qmd).
